§10.5.2 Form Reading Order

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

forms-form-reading-order · forms

✅ Normative

The fields of a form MUST be ordered by the form's printed indexing scheme — its ids — rather than by column-first or row-first geometry.

A form's ids are its intended order. Where lettered and numbered fields share a page, one scheme MUST be read through, then the other, rather than sweeping across the page and interleaving them.

An id sequence stays contiguous

  • Fields whose ids run in sequence MUST stay together and in order, with no un-id'd field between them.
  • Unlabelled fields MUST be placed around the sequence, not inside it. A 1099-MISC is the standard case.

Sections do not interleave

Fields from different printed sections MUST NOT be mixed, even when they sit side by side on the page.

Where this differs from block reading order

Reading Order§5.9 orders regions on a page the way a person reads them. This rule orders fields within a form, and the form's own numbering overrides visual position when the two disagree — which on a dense tax form they routinely do. Where a group of fields prints no ids, the order of Reading Order§5.9 applies.
